page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers for both compute and memory throughput. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1100.49 and a multi-core score of 2931.93, both categorized in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show 163.82 GB/sec for cached small blocks, but this drops to 20.19 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Geekbench scores also reflect these limitations, with a single-core score of 918.0 and a multi-core score of 1990.0, indicating constrained processing capabilities for intensive tasks.

The primary trade-off of the ecs.se1.xlarge is its high memory allocation relative to its modest compute performance. While it offers a cost-effective profile for memory-heavy workloads that do not require high-speed processing, it is poorly suited for CPU-intensive calculations or high-throughput web serving. This instance is best utilized for workloads such as caching layers, Redis databases, and lightweight memory-bound applications.
